Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  May 1, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on May 1, 2025. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio
  Padilla - District 2, Cynthia McLemore - District 3
  Absent:  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large, Commissioner
  Christopher Beck - District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Teresa Estrada  Assistant Director
  Jack Mooring  Tree Maintenance Supervisor
  Kesha Brady  Food Services Program Manager
  Kaderick Burns  Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner
Padilla that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on April 3,
2025, be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:

Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Padilla, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Tree Maintenance Supervisor, Jack Mooring,
reported the following: Park Maintenance – Newly renovated picnic shelters at Edward
Vincent Park are now open and available for public use. Tree Maintenance – The City’s
tree contractor West Coast Arborists (WCA) is nearly half way done with trimming 2,000
of the city’s ficus trees. 1,600 Chinese elm trees are set to be trimmed starting next week.
They will also start trimming palm trees in June. The City’s crews are making good progress
in trimming grids that were not scheduled for trimming until 2027, the same with weekly
service request. Graffiti Abatement – A chart that reflects all graffiti removals for the

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

current fiscal year, from October 1, 2024, to April 30, 2025 was handed out. Graffiti activity
increased significantly over the past month, with District 4 experiencing at least 500 new
tagging. Our team responded by removing nearly 1,000 more instances of graffiti
compared to the previous month. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.
REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Kaderick Burns reported the following:
Touch a Truck Event - Get ready for a day of family fun at the City of Inglewood’s first
ever; Touch a Truck event! This exciting, hands-on experience gives kids (and kids at
heart!) the chance to explore the big trucks, emergency vehicles, and heavy equipment
that help keep our city running. Bring the whole family for a unique, educational, and
interactive outdoor event you will not want to miss!

Date: Saturday, May 3, 2025
Time: 11:00 a.m. - 1:00 p.m.
Location: Rogers Park - 400 West Beach Avenue, Inglewood, CA 90302

For additional information, contact the Parks, Recreation and Community Services
Department at (310) 412-8750. Memorial Day Service - We are pleased to share
information about the City’s upcoming Memorial Day Service. The service will take place
on Monday, May 26, 2025, at 11:00 a.m. here at City Hall at the Memorial Obelisk. This
meaningful event honors the brave men and women who have served our country, and
we truly hope you can attend if your schedule permits. Inglewood Youth Sports - The
Inglewood Youth Sports League continues to bring exciting athletic programming to the
community. The spring season brings the Dodgers Dreamteam league serving T-Ball (ages
5-6) and Coach Pitch (ages 7-8). The league is completely full with 196 players, 16 teams,
and 22 coaches. The season begins playing games the week of May 5 and will run through
June 7. Game days are Thursday evenings with 5:45 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. game times while
Saturday games begin at 9:00 a.m. and end around 2:00 p.m. We also welcome back the
sport of Track and Field to Inglewood this Spring. We have 140 boys and girls ages 5 to 14
ready to compete in a four meet season. The first meet is this Sunday, April 27 at Carson
High School, which will feature competitors from various cities. The season will conclude
with the SCMAF Finals on May 31 at Warren High School in Downey. Please check the IYSL
website to get the latest information regarding youth sports. Go Inglewood! Splish Slash -
Our Annual Splish Splash event will take place on Saturday, May 17, 2025 from 11:00 a.m.
to 3:00 p.m. at the Edward Vincent Jr. Park Swim Complex. Splish Splash brings awareness
to all water safety (indoor & outdoor) and represents the opening of the pool for the
summer season. The event will include water safety demonstrations, facility tours, music,
food, vendors, raffles, giveaways, safety tips, and more. We look forward to seeing you on
Saturday, May 17. For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our
city sports website at https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Program Manager, Kesha Brady reported
the following: Senior Center Operations - Our Senior Center is packed with more seniors
than ever, as we continue to grow our participation numbers, as well as increase our
offerings. Grace Farwell of the organization Helping Elderly Live Productively or H.E.L.P. for
short will be presenting on the topic of helping seniors improve their ability to do daily
tasks and live independently on May 2 and May 23. On May 14, students from St. Mary’s
Academy will attend our jewelry making class and assist our seniors. Mercedes Aguirre of
the LA County Department of Mental Health will be conduction a presentation on Elder
Financial Exploitation on May 19. On May 29, Amy Lozano from City of Inglewood
Emergency Preparedness will be conduction a presentation on “How to heal a wound”.
Opicacares will be presenting a caregiver resources presentation on May 28. On May 8, we
will be showing the movie “Life”. On May 9, we will be having a Mother’s Day celebration
from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., and on May 29, we will be having our dance party event
from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Senior Nutrition - The Senior Center serves approximately 460
seniors per week through home delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate
meals. We continue to offer fresh produce weekly in partnership with the Social Justice
Learning Institute. Our numbers continue to climb weekly in program participation and we
look forward to serving all of our seniors. Child and Adult Care Food Program - The Child
and Adult Care Food Program, informally CACFP, serves meals to youth 18 years old and
under and operates at Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The program's
hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks
from 4:30 PM - 5:00 PM. We serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week.
Senior Transportation - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to provide
trips to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. We will be
participating in the upcoming Touch-A-Truck event being held at Roger’s Park on May 3,
2025, where our Trolley will be on display for youth to see up close and personal and to
enjoy. We plan to provide dialysis trips to those on the upcoming city holiday in
observance of Memorial Day on Monday May 25, 2025. As always, we look forward to
continuing to provide the best possible service for our seniors and disabled community.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Assistant Director, Teresa Estrada reported on the following: 4th
Annual Women’s Rock Empowerment Event - the City of Inglewood is proud to present
the 4th Annual Women’s Rock Empowerment Event Saturday, May 3, 2025, at the
Inglewood Senior Center. This impactful event is dedicated to uplifting and empowering
women through a variety of workshops and sessions centered on financial literacy,
leadership development, mental health, and overall well-being. Attendees will have the
opportunity to gain valuable tools, connect with like-minded individuals, and hear from
dynamic speakers who are leaders in their fields. Join us as we celebrate the strength,
resilience, and accomplishments of women in our community. Mid-Year Budget Review -
The City of Inglewood’s Budget Office is currently conducting its annual mid-year budget
review. This essential process provides an opportunity to evaluate the City’s financial

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

performance by comparing actual revenues and expenditures against the adopted budget
for the current fiscal year. Based on these insights, the department will propose
adjustments to ensure continued fiscal responsibility and alignment with strategic goals.
The mid-year review supports transparency, accountability, and effective resource
management throughout the City’s operations.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Ayana Taylor, Inglewood resident, attended summer camp as a kid.
She expressed that she did not like Edward Vincent Park before but has seen how it has
changed and that she loves the new restrooms.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Denmon commended the Graffiti Division.
Teresa Estrada acknowledged and thanked Commissioner Padilla and Commissioner Beck
for coming out to the basketball championship games at the Intuit Dome’s practice gym.
Commissioner McLemore thanked staff for their reports. Commissioner Padilla thanked
Ms. Estrada for the acknowledgement.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:27 p.m.
